subject: interior-design
intro: Interior design leads into the practices that shape the rooms people live, work and heal in — planning the space, specifying the finishes, drawing the construction set and running the job.

roles.title: Interior Designers
roles.what: Plan, design and furnish the internal space of rooms or buildings, creating layouts that are practical, safe and suited to the client's purpose, from first concept to the final installation.
roles.where: Unit 1's programming and space planning is the heart of the role, with unit 2's anthropometrics, ergonomics and universal design supplying the human-centred standards the work is judged against.

roles.title: Set and Exhibit Designers
roles.what: Design special exhibits and sets for film, video, television and theatre: study the script or brief, research the right period and style, and work with directors to build environments that read on camera or on the floor.
roles.where: Unit 1's elements and principles and unit 3's colour, lighting and acoustic design transfer directly, while unit 4's finish selection and specification becomes choosing materials that survive production schedules.

roles.title: Architectural and Civil Drafters
roles.what: Prepare the detailed drawings and plans architects and engineers rely on, turning design decisions into precise construction documents for buildings and site work.
roles.where: Unit 5's construction drawings, building systems basics and codes and regulations are exactly this job: documenting an interior design so contractors can build it to standard.
